newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay markets unaffected by telecom stir-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bombay markets unaffected by telecom stir-dealers.

text.p: Stock markets in India's commercial hub of Bombay were unaffected on Wednesday by a nationwide telecommunications strike but the stir hit some banks, brokers and dealers said.
"Business is smooth," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities. "We have had no problem."
But bank dealers said the stir, which affected mostly local telephone lines, hit trading in the inter-bank call money and securities market and pushed up call rates.
"Borrowers were desperate to cover their position," a dealer at a government-owned bank said. "Few lenders could be reached."
Call rates rose to 10.0 percent in afternoon trade from 8.75 percent at the start, dealers said.
About one million workers from state-owned telecommunications and postal departments began an indefinite nationwide strike over a wage dispute on Wednesday.
A spokesman for Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd, India's state-controlled firm responsible for all overseas communication, said the strike had no impact on its operations.
The Bombay Stock Exchange was unaffected. Its top-30 stock index was up 81.97 points, or 2.54 percent, higher at 3,309.10 in latest deals.
Officials at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) said the stir had no impact on trading so far.
The 50-stock NSE index was up 26.37 points, or 2.87 percent, up at 945.37.
